name: Ecofeminism
summary: Ecofeminism holds that the domination of women and the domination of nonhuman nature are linked, through patriarchal conceptual dualisms (man/woman, culture/nature, mind/body) and through institutions such as capitalism, mechanistic science and patriarchal religion. It seeks an ecological, care-based and often subsistence-oriented alternative to growth-driven development, and it is expressed through grassroots women's environmental activism and anti-militarism. Strands differ on whether the women-nature link is socially constructed or reflects embodied experience, and on spirituality.
scope: The mainstream academic and activist ecofeminism since d'Eaubonne's 1974 coinage, centred on Karen Warren's logic of domination, Carolyn Merchant, Val Plumwood, and the materialist/Global South strand of Vandana Shiva and Maria Mies. It spans the social/socialist, vegetarian and spiritual strands; where they differ, answers follow the socialist and Shiva-Mies core and mark contested points low.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The Stanford entry says a failure to care about animal suffering or the destruction of the planet is a moral wrong on ecofeminist care ethics.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Shiva presents capitalist commodity growth as maldevelopment that destroys the potential of nature and women to produce life, rather than as a progressive force.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Shiva presents colonial and post-colonial 'development' as maldevelopment that destroyed subsistence economies and made poverty where there had been none.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Shiva describes colonial rule as draining resources and impoverishing the colonised, especially women, and the Stanford entry reports her account of maldevelopment beginning with colonisation.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Shiva states that commodity production as the prime economic activity means 'more commodities and more cash mean less life' in nature and society.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Warren lists heterosexism among the unjustified 'isms of domination', which excludes criminalising same-sex relations.

decide-locally.rationale: Shiva wants control of seeds, forests and commons in the hands of those who provide sustenance and objects to privatising commons that local communities share.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Warren names the 'logic of domination', the premise that superiority justifies subordination, as the root of racism and ethnocentrism and rejects it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The Stanford entry defines ecofeminist philosophy as exploring the connections between the unjustified dominations of women and nature, and d'Eaubonne's founding book and Britannica's definition make the same link.

experts-over-public.rationale: The Stanford entry shows rural women, not the Western-trained forester, as the real experts on forest use, and Shiva defends local women's knowledge against reductionist expertise.

free-trade.rationale: Shiva argues the export-crop model pre-empts land, credit and water for export markets and increases hunger, with profits flowing to corporations.

gm-crops.rationale: Shiva argues genetic engineering and biotechnology are masculinist, corporate technologies that destroy seeds as sources of life, and that ecological intercropping makes them unnecessary.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Shiva says that after independence new national elites continued the colonial exploitation in the name of GNP growth, so political change alone left the economic domination in place.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Warren treats sexism, racism, classism and the domination of nature as 'isms of domination' with shared conceptual roots, and Britannica says contemporary ecofeminism acknowledges the effects of race, class, ethnicity and sexuality.

limit-growth.rationale: Shiva calls the economic growth measured by GNP 'maldevelopment': more commodities and cash mean less life in nature and in society, and growth hides the destruction of nature's and women's sustenance.

local-production.rationale: Shiva describes the sustenance economy as built on local knowledge, locally recycled inputs and 'local consumption for local needs', against specialised production for export.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Shiva argues the commodity and cash economy destroys natural cycles and denies basic needs, and that profits from market-led export agriculture flow to corporations while the hungry are left out.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Shiva holds that each living thing in the forest is 'valuable in itself', and the Stanford entry presents ecofeminist ethics as caring about nature and animals for their own sake.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Warren's oppressive conceptual framework conceives power and privilege so that they systematically advantage the 'Ups' (men) over the 'Downs' (women), and materialist ecofeminists describe male-biased ownership systematically disadvantaging women.

power-shapes-accepted-knowledge.rationale: The Stanford entry shows Western forestry making women's knowledge invisible, and Shiva argues reductionist science is tied to a particular ideology of capitalist patriarchy rather than being neutral.

production-for-use.rationale: Shiva contrasts the sustenance economy, producing for basic needs, with commodity production for cash, which she says destroys nature's and women's capacity to meet needs.

property-fundamental.rationale: Shiva argues privatising commons closes off access for the poorest and destroys sustenance, which runs against treating private property as very hard to override.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Warren lists racism among the 'isms of domination' that rest on an unjustified logic of domination, so restricting immigration by race is that kind of domination.

racial-franchise.rationale: Warren lists racism among the 'isms of domination' that rest on an unjustified logic of domination, so reserving the vote to one ethnic group is that kind of domination.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Warren lists racism among the 'isms of domination' that rest on an unjustified logic of domination, so a law enforcing racial segregation is a form of that unjustified domination.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Warren lists racism among the 'isms of domination' that rest on an unjustified logic of domination, so removing indigenous peoples from their lands is that kind of domination, and the Stanford entry reports ecofeminists backing indigenous forest knowledge and use.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Warren lists racism among the 'isms of domination' that rest on an unjustified logic of domination, so removing members of other ethnic groups is that kind of domination (ethnocentrism is on her list too).

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Shiva argues modern science and technology are tied to violence, profit and capitalist patriarchy, and that biotechnology is sold as a miracle answer that deepens the problems.

technology-design-reflects-political-int.rationale: Shiva argues science and technology have become inseparable inside the scientific military-industrial complex of capitalist patriarchy, so that technology serves a particular social model.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Materialist ecofeminists in the Stanford entry hold that male-biased ownership of the means of production disadvantages women, and Shiva links maldevelopment to the feminisation of poverty.

women-suffrage.rationale: Warren names sexism, the subordination of women by men, as an unjustified domination, which excludes denying women political rights.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Shiva describes economic growth as a new colonialism draining resources away from those who need them most, and the debt crisis as indebtedness of peoples and nations.

missingStatements.text: The domination of women and the domination of nature are connected and should be ended together.
missingStatements.rationale: The core ecofeminist claim, in Warren's logic of domination and d'Eaubonne's founding argument; no existing statement captures the link itself.

missingStatements.text: Women's unpaid and subsistence work sustaining life is real wealth that economic growth measures leave out.
missingStatements.rationale: Shiva argues GNP counts the money economy while hiding the wealth of nature and of women's sustenance production.

missingStatements.text: Modern science's reductionist method treats nature as something to master and has served domination.
missingStatements.rationale: Merchant, Mies and Shiva all make this critique of mechanistic science.

notes: Answers rest on the Stanford Encyclopedia entry (Warren), Shiva's Staying Alive, the Environment & Society Portal note on d'Eaubonne and Britannica. Strands differ on spirituality and on whether the women-nature link is constructed or embodied, so those statements are null. Themes searched: economy, ecology, technology, world, culture, government, society; government, liberty and means statements are mostly null because these sources state no position. Wikipedia (s1) is kept only for older history entries.
